chunks: Ali, from his father, from Hannan, from his father, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), said:
Vinegar of wine was mentioned in his presence, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It kills the insects of the belly and strengthens the mouth.'
ai.seo_question: What are the benefits of vinegar of wine according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) highlights the medicinal efficacy of wine vinegar (khal al-khamr), noting its ability to eliminate intestinal parasites and strengthen the oral cavity. This narration is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between the vinegar of wine and other vinegars, particularly in debates regarding whether the transformation (istihlal) of wine into vinegar renders it pure and consumable, thereby affirming its utility in traditional Islamic medicine.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Hannan, from his father, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
The wine vinegar was mentioned in his<sup>asws</sup> presence, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It kills the insects of the belly and strengthens the mouth’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali has narrated from his father from Hanan ibn Sadir from his father who has said the following:

“Once, vinegar of wine (clean grape juice with vinegar in it placed in the sun to turn the whole thing into vinegar) was mentioned before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. He (the Imam) said, ‘It kills dawab (the insects) in the belly and strengthens the mouth (the teeth).’”
